label: Propofol PK — Kataria (pediatric, 1994)

extraction.tier_rationale: Single pediatric derivation cohort (n=53, ages 3-11 y). Central value shown at a 23 kg reference child.
The age-dependent V2 term is the Kataria model's distinctive feature and the field most needing human PDF confirmation (covariate equations are where transcription errors hide).

known_failure_modes.condition: use in adults (a pediatric model extrapolated upward)
known_failure_modes.behavior: Kataria was derived only in children 3-11 y; applying it to adults extrapolates beyond its cohort and the age term in V2 is no longer validated.

known_failure_modes.condition: very young / low weight (below the derivation cohort)
known_failure_modes.behavior: V2 = 0.78*WGT + 3.1*AGE - 16 can approach or cross zero for the smallest/youngest children, where the linear age/weight terms were not derived.

extraction.tier_rationale: Single pediatric derivation cohort (53 healthy children, 3-11 y); the canonical pediatric propofol model that the literature routinely compares head-to-head with Paedfusor ('Kataria vs Paedfusor'). Weight-proportional volumes/clearances with an age term on V2. PK-only (the 1994 disposition study published no ke0). Kernel transcribed from the standard published parameter set (same STANPUMP/Shafer lineage as Minto); review_status remains UNVERIFIED pending human confirmation of every covariate equation against the primary PDF, especially the age term in V2.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched open-source reproductions, primary-paper PubMed abstracts, and/or the tci R package source, then numerically compared each curated value against the fetched values
sources: kataria-1994-propofol-pediatric (primary; results table paywalled, abstract read)
source_review.notes: All 6 covariate coefficients (V1 0.41*WGT, V2 0.78*WGT+3.1*AGE-16, V3 6.9*WGT, Cl1 0.035*WGT, Cl2 0.077*WGT, Cl3 0.026*WGT) confirmed against two independent reproductions; the distinctive age term on V2 corroborated by the primary PubMed abstract ('age significantly improved V2'). Pediatric 3-11 y. HUMAN ITEM: confirm against the primary Anesthesiology results table.

notes: Completes the spec's named pediatric pair (Kataria/Paedfusor). PK-only (ke0=0): the pediatric model-divergence view compares Kataria vs Paedfusor on plasma concentration. Volumes/clearances at a 23 kg, 7 y reference child; the kernel recomputes them per patient from the covariate equations.
